claim_1.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from 56 vaccinated individuals showed robust neutralizing antibody responses against the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 and a tenfold-lower response against the B.1.351 variant after secondary vaccination compared to primary vaccination.

sources.quote: BNT162b2 vaccination also induced a neutralizing antibody response against the B.1.351 variant of concern, albeit at a tenfold-lower magnitude than against the wild-type WA1/2020 (WA1) strain ( Fig. 1c )

claim_2.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from 56 vaccinated individuals showed significant increases in anti-S IgG titers after secondary vaccination compared to primary vaccination.

comparison.finding: significant increases in anti-S IgG titers after secondary vaccination compared to primary vaccination

claim_3.claim: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 vaccinated individuals showed intermediate monocyte frequencies increased two days after the primary vaccination (day 2) and substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination (day 23) compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14 + CD16 + monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination, and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination ( Fig. 2b ).

comparison.finding: Intermediate monocyte frequencies increased two days after the primary vaccination compared to baseline.
Intermediate monocyte frequencies were substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination compared to baseline.

claim_4.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed IFNγ and CXCL10 concentrations increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination and further increased after secondary immunization.

sources.quote: Of the 67 cytokines detected, the concentration of 2 cytokines (IFNγ and CXCL10) were increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination ( Fig. 2e left). Similar to our observations on intermediate monocytes and pSTAT1 and pSTAT3, the concentrations of these cytokines were increased even further after the secondary immunization ( Fig. 2e right).

comparison.finding: IFNγ and CXCL10 concentrations increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination

claim_5.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1, with significant enrichment of interferon and antiviral response modules after secondary vaccination.

sources.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response, with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1 ( Fig. 3a ); this is consistent with the increased markers of innate immunity detected by both CyTOF and Olink ( Fig. 2 ).

comparison.finding: fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1, with significant enrichment of interferon and antiviral response modules

claim_6.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 6 individuals showed the emergence of cluster C8, enriched in interferon-stimulated genes, increased almost 100-fold one day after secondary vaccination (day 22) compared to one day after primary vaccination (day 1).

sources.quote: These cells uniquely expressed interferon-stimulated genes, including WARS (also known as WARS1 ), GBP1 , IFI30 and IFITM3 , and constituted about 0.01% of the Lin − HLA-DR + population on day 1 after primary vaccination but increased almost 100-fold to about 1% one day after secondary vaccination ( Fig. 4c ).

comparison.finding: emergence of cluster C8, enriched in interferon-stimulated genes, increased almost 100-fold
